# fourthirtyfive

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/kuriwaki/fourthirtyfive/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/kuriwaki/fourthirtyfive/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

Maintainer: Shiro Kuriwaki

Contributors: Zoya Ahmer, Zachary Donnini, Cory McCartan

Copyright holders: Downballot (some data)


`fourthirtyfive` is a package that provides shapefiles and other data for the 435 congressional districts, gathering good ideas from various authors.

The coverage badges show Congress start years for bundled datasets on `main`.
Use `cd_available()` for the full guide, including historical geographic boundaries.

## Installation

You can install the development version of fourthirtyfive from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
remotes::install_github("kuriwaki/fourthirtyfive")
```


## Example

Use the `cd_` accessors to retrieve district data. Type `cd_` in RStudio to discover the family with autocomplete.

```{r example}
library(fourthirtyfive)
```

| Accessor | Returns |
|---|---|
| `cd_boundaries()` | Geographic district boundaries as an `sf` object |
| `cd_dotmap()` | Dodged district points as an `sf` object |
| `cd_hexmap()` | District hex cartograms as an `sf` object |
| `cd_names()` | Descriptive geographical district names as a tibble |
| `cd_available()` | A CLI summary and an invisible availability table |

Check the available products and periods without downloading any maps:

```{r availability}
cd_available()
```

Use `cd_available(quiet = TRUE)` to get just the table.


We are building several types of maps. First, the **dotmap** is where one CD is treated as point. We use the centroid of the actual map, and dodge it so that crowded points do not completely overlap with each other.

```{r dotmap}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

cd_dotmap(2023) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = shp_states) +
  geom_sf(size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_void()
```

Dotmaps are also available as bundled datasets:

```{r dotmap-data}
shp_dot_2023
```


We also provide **hexmaps** (i.e., maps that present CDs as combinations of hexagons) for all years. The 2013-2025 maps are sourced from the Downballot's hex map shapefiles (<https://the-db.co/maps>). The 2005-2011 maps are generated with Cory McCartan's [hexmap](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/hexmap) package.

```{r hexmap}
cd_hexmap(2023) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf() +
  theme_void() +
  labs(caption = "Map Source: https://the-db.co/maps")
```

Note: An earlier version of these hex maps was provided in the [`donnermap`](https://github.com/kuriwaki/donnermap) package. Those shapefiles used unprojected coordinates that do not match the coordinate system of the other hex maps here. The hex maps in `fourthirtyfive` use the projected Web Mercator versions (`wm` suffix) from the Downballot.



We do not store actual CD shapefiles, but we provide a function to draw these from either the Census or Jeff Lewis's historical shapefiles.

```{r load-boundaries, include = FALSE}
suppressMessages(cd_shps <- cd_boundaries(congress = 118))
```

```{r boundaries-example, eval=FALSE}
cd_shps <- cd_boundaries(congress = 118)
```

```{r boundaries}
cd_shps |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf() +
  theme_void()
```

Compare Tennessee's district boundaries for the 119th and 120th Congresses.
The maps use the same extent and district colors, with the 119th Congress above
the 120th.

```{r tn-boundaries, fig.width=9, fig.height=6.5, message=FALSE}
library(patchwork)

tn_boundaries <- cd_boundaries(congress = c(119, 120), state = "TN")
tn_extent <- st_bbox(tn_boundaries)

plot_tn <- function(congress_number, title) {
  tn_boundaries |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$congress == congress_number) |>
    ggplot(aes(fill = cd)) +
    geom_sf(color = "white", linewidth = 0.35) +
    geom_sf_text(aes(label = stringr::str_remove(cd, "^TN-0?")), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3", guide = "none") +
    coord_sf(
      xlim = unname(tn_extent[c("xmin", "xmax")]),
      ylim = unname(tn_extent[c("ymin", "ymax")]),
      expand = FALSE
    ) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13))
}

tn_119 <- plot_tn(119, "119th Congress (2025-2026)")
tn_120 <- plot_tn(120, "120th Congress (2027-2028)")

(tn_119 / tn_120) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Tennessee congressional districts",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Census Bureau via tigris. 119th: 2024 cartographic boundaries;\n120th: 2026 TIGER/Line boundaries, simplified for display. Colors identify district numbers."
  )
```

### Interactive comparisons

Use `cd_mapbox()` to overlay one to three Congresses on a single interactive map.
Select a state or a district, and use the map's layer controls to switch Congresses
on and off. City boundaries are absent by default; select one or two incorporated
cities to highlight only those cities in magenta.

Tennessee's 119th and 120th Congresses, with Memphis highlighted:

```{r tn-interactive, eval=FALSE}
cd_mapbox(state = "TN", congress = c(119, 120), cities = "Memphis")
```

![Tennessee with 119th-Congress boundaries in blue, 120th-Congress boundaries in orange, and Memphis in magenta.](man/figures/README-tn-interactive.png)

Zoom to Memphis while retaining both Congress layers:

```{r memphis-interactive, eval=FALSE}
cd_mapbox(
  state = "TN", congress = c(119, 120), cities = "Memphis",
  zoom_to_cities = TRUE
)
```

![Memphis city boundaries in magenta with the 119th and 120th congressional districts overlaid.](man/figures/README-memphis-interactive.png)

City outlines use the same 2026 Census geography in both views. District boundary
detail varies across Congresses, so small differences at street scale may reflect
cartographic generalization. The camera control saves the current map as a PNG.

#### Mapbox setup and free usage

Install the optional mapping package:

```{r install-mapgl, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("mapgl")
```

Create a [Mapbox account](https://account.mapbox.com/auth/signup/) and copy its
public access token (`pk.`) from the [Access Tokens page](https://console.mapbox.com/account/access-tokens/).
Add the following line to your user `.Renviron` file, replace the placeholder,
and restart R:

```text
MAPBOX_PUBLIC_TOKEN="pk.YOUR_PUBLIC_TOKEN"
```

Check configuration without printing the token:

```{r check-mapbox, eval=FALSE}
nzchar(Sys.getenv("MAPBOX_PUBLIC_TOKEN"))
```

As verified on October 25, 2026, Mapbox's **card-free trial allows 5,000 map loads
per month**. Adding a payment method enables pay as you go, with **50,000 free map
loads per month and billable overages**. These are different account modes; check
the [trial limits](https://docs.mapbox.com/accounts/guides/signup/) and
[current pricing](https://www.mapbox.com/pricing).

Each viewer initializes one map, even with three Congress overlays. Reloading it
creates another load; panning, zooming, and toggling layers within it do not.
See [Mapbox's map-load definition](https://docs.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/guides/pricing/).
Monitor usage in the Mapbox Console: notification thresholds
[do not cap spending](https://docs.mapbox.com/accounts/faq/can-i-set-up-a-cap-for-monthly-spending/).
For token scopes, publication restrictions, and more setup details, run
`help("mapbox-setup", package = "fourthirtyfive")`.


We also provide a dataset of the **descriptive names** of each district (e.g., calling AZ-01 in the 110th congressional district "Phoenix exurbs, Prescott, and Flagstaff"). 
These use [Daily
Kos](https://www.dailykos.com/stories/2022/8/8/2113098/-The-Daily-Kos-Elections-naming-guide-to-this-decade-s-new-congressional-districts) namings. Zachary Donnini named 2008-2010 congressional districts.


```{r district-names}
cd_names(2007)
```

The same district names are available as a bundled dataset:

```{r district-names-data, eval = FALSE}
info_2007
```



## Data format

We name the datasets (`shp_dot_**`, `info_**`) by the year of the congress.

|Object | Congress | Years in Session | Year Elected | Year up for Election | 
|-------|----------|-------|---------------|----------|
|`**_2005` | 109th | 2005-2006 | 2004 | 2006 |
|`**_2007` | 110th | 2007-2008 | 2006 | 2008 |
|`**_2009` | 111th | 2009-2010 | 2008 | 2010 |
|`**_2011` | 112th | 2011-2012 | 2010 | 2012 |
|`**_2013` | 113th | 2013-2014 | 2012 | 2014 | 
|`**_2015` | 114th | 2015-2016 | 2014 | 2016 |
|`**_2017` | 115th | 2017-2018 | 2016 | 2018 |
|`**_2019` | 116th | 2019-2020 | 2018 | 2020 |
|`**_2021` | 117th | 2021-2022 | 2020 | 2022 |
|`**_2023` | 118th | 2023-2024 | 2022 | 2024 |
|`**_2025` | 119th | 2025-2026 | 2024 | 2026 |
|`**_2027` | 120th | 2027-2028 | 2026 | 2028 |
